newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's IRI details Stet unit sale.
newsitem.headline: Italy's IRI details Stet unit sale.

text.p: Italian state industrial holding group IRI said Seat, the yellow pages publishing unit of state telecoms group Stet, will be quoted on the Milan stock exchange after being spun off from its parent.

IRI said in a statement that ordinary and savings shares of the future public company Seat SpA "for which a Bourse listing is expected" will be attributed to Stet shareholders "in the same proportion as the respective stakes in Stet's capital."
As a result, IRI said it will hold 61.27 percent of Seat SpA's ordinary capital and 0.93 percent of its savings capital.

The statement said the sale of IRI's Seat stake will be carried out parallel to Seat's separation from Stet and is expected to be by a competitive procedure through the publication of advertisements inviting offers from interested purchasers.

The statement followed an IRI board meeting which instituted the process of spinning off Seat. The government last month ordered IRI to evaluate the Seat sale before the sale of Stet itself in February or March 1997.
Board member Piero Gnudi told reporters after the meeting that the Seat spinoff was expected to take three or four months to complete.
